a2_threshold: From a foot away the great door is dwarf bronze laid over iron, standing open exactly a hand's width, and the air coming out of the gap is warm and smells of lamp oil and wet stone. The edge of the gap has been worn smooth at shoulder height by traffic, which is not something a door does to itself.
a2_gap: You go through sideways, one at a time, with packs passed through afterwards, and Dellach manages it last and worst of anybody. While Odd is still in the gap the door moves a finger's width inward, unhurriedly, on no draught whatsoever, and then stops again as though it had merely been thinking.
a2_lever: The poleaxe haft goes into the gap with Dellach's entire weight behind it, and the door comes open two feet with a groan that travels down into the hill and keeps travelling for longer than seems reasonable. There is a pause afterwards. Then something a long way below begins to count.
a2_shield: The Warden's shield comes off the post in two blows and turns over heavily in your hands. On the inside face, somebody with plenty of time and no light at all has scratched three lines with the tongue of a belt buckle. Eight hold, nine counts, do not answer it when it uses your name, and the lettering deteriorates badly toward the end.
a2_chute: The spoil chute lies on the hill's flank, a throat of loose scree dropping forty feet into complete darkness, cut by dwarves who wanted somewhere to throw waste. The stones at the lip have been polished by something coming up and down it since. Nothing has thrown waste out of here for nine hundred years.
a2_chute_rope: Forty feet of rope work in the dark gets everybody down to the bottom with skinned palms and nothing worse than that. The mule stays tethered above, expressing his opinion of the arrangement at considerable and sustained volume for as long as anybody can still hear him. Cold water is waiting at the foot of the chute, and it is deeper than the lamplight suggested.
a2_chute_kettle: Kettle goes down first on a single line with two whistles agreed for clear, which is the arrangement she always insists on. The whistles do not come. There is nothing at all for six minutes, which is four minutes longer than the arrangement allows for, and then one whistle, very quietly.
a2_sump: The sump at the chute's foot is a tank of cut stone holding waist-deep black water, with an iron grate at the far end admitting to the vault proper. A quantity of material has collected against the grate over the past several months. Most of it is cloth, and most of the cloth is unmistakably Warden issue.
a2_grate: What the grate has kept: a Warden's tally-iron on a thong, a sodden dispatch bag with the writing gone, and a boot with the foot still laced into it. Nyre takes charge of the boot before anybody can make a joke about it, which is probably why nobody does.
a2_dark: The dry gallery is unlit, and it smells like a larder because that is what it is. Eleven bodies have been stacked with genuine care in a side bay, and four pale drinkers sleep among them, long-limbed and ribbed like greyhounds, their hands folded neatly in front of them like men at prayer.
a2_burn: Oil, flint, and a side bay that goes up like a hayrick. Three drinkers die in the fire without ever properly waking, and the fourth goes away down the gallery screaming in a register that hurts the teeth. The smoke follows the company for an hour and announces its position for two.
a2_quiet: Eleven minutes of moving past sleeping drinkers at the pace of a minute hand, with Ilsabet laying a salt line behind each footfall. The fourth one opens its eyes as the last of you goes by, considers the situation without moving at all, and then visibly decides not to bother.
a2_postern: The mason's postern sits round the hill's shoulder: a dwarf door about the size of a coffin lid, sealed with lead and inscribed with mason's marks. Beside it, cut into the living rock, is a tally of nine strokes, and the dust from the ninth stroke has not yet been washed out by rain.
a2_tally: Read closely, the tally is nine strokes with the ninth struck through, and below it a second hand has kept a running count in the hundreds, grouped in nines. The lower groups go back further than the lead in the door has been cold. Ilsabet stops translating before she reaches the bottom.
a2_postern_open: An hour of quiet work: lead cut away in curls, mason's marks answered one at a time in Ilsabet's chalk, and the door finally opening inward on cold air. The corridor beyond has dust on the floor that nothing with hands has walked through for a very long time.
a2_postern_break: The postern breaks in four blows, which the hill repeats back to you for considerably longer than four blows deserve. Then a lamp appears at the far end of the corridor, coming up at walking pace, held by somebody who does not hurry, does not call out, and does not appear to be armed.
a2_hall: The weighing floor of Kar Duhn is a hall of standing scales, with nine iron-bound chests ranged along one wall and every one of them open and empty. The floor is a mosaic showing a door held shut by nine hands. Three ways lead on: the barracks arch, the counting-room passage, and a gallery from which the smell of fresh lamp oil is unmistakable.
a2_mosaic: Under the dust the mosaic resolves into something specific: eight hands laid flat against a door of nine irons, and a ninth hand standing apart in front of it holding a tally-board. A border of dwarf letters runs the whole way round the design, worn shallow by nine centuries of boots.
a2_mosaic_read: Ilsabet reads the border aloud in careful dwarf, and it becomes clear within a line and a half that this is not a dedication. The door is not a lock but a lid: eight hands to hold it down, and one hand to keep the count and to bring what is owed on the appointed day. The final clause of the border is a price, payable in nines, in perpetuity.
a2_barracks: The garrison barracks holds forty bunks made up to inspection standard, kit stowed, boots paired at the foot of each bed. The far third of the room has been walled off from floor to ceiling with a barricade of shields and bunk timber. The barricade was built from this side, by people who then stayed on this side.
a2_wall: Opened just enough to see through, the barricade gives up its contents. Eleven Wardens are seated shoulder to shoulder along the wall behind it, drained to paper, hands folded, boots off and paired neatly beside each of them. The fourth man from the left is slowly turning his head toward the gap.
a2_wall_mercy: One clean stroke from Dellach, and afterwards Nyre sets the man's boots straight and writes his name in her book from the tag at his collar. She says the words at half volume because there is not time for the whole rite, and she notes that fact down as well.
a2_wall_ask: The question is asked, and it is answered in numbers, patiently, in the manner of a clerk responding to a query about an account. Eight, it says, and then a pause of exactly the right length, and then eight again. When Nyre asks who the ninth is, the head turns further round on its neck and looks directly at the company for the first time.
a2_chest: The sergeant's chest is unlocked, because there was eventually nothing left worth locking. Inside: a duty roster with nine names struck out in identical ink, an unmarked Warden key-iron blank, and a bottle of paymaster's brandy with two fingers gone out of the neck.
a2_roster: The roster reads badly on the walk: nine names struck out on nine consecutive days, the last of them the paymaster's own. Against every struck name somebody has written a single word in the margin, and Ilsabet says the word is the dwarf term used in accounts for tendered.
a2_blank: An unmarked key-iron, the same length and gauge as the ones the door is carved with, entirely blank where the tally should be cut. Ilsabet takes it off you, wraps it in salt-cloth, and puts it in her own pack without offering any explanation for why she is smiling.
a2_bottle: Two fingers of paymaster's brandy each, which is not much and turns out to be exactly enough. The company stands in a dead man's barracks drinking a dead man's drink, and everybody's hands come back to them within about ten minutes, which is worth more than the brandy cost anybody.
a2_rest: Four hours of shifts on made beds in a barracks that smells strongly of other men's boots. Nobody sleeps well and everybody sleeps, and at the end of it the company is capable of having the day it is about to have, which was not true before.
a2_counting: The counting room holds a table forty feet long with nine balances set out in a row along it, and the winter pay-ledger lies open at its final page beneath a lamp that is still burning. In the lock of the ninth chest a key-iron stands where a hand let go of it and did not come back.
a2_lastpage: The last page shows a winter's pay entered in full and balanced against nothing at all, with nine names tendered in a clerk's failing hand. At the foot of the column, in a different pen and pressed hard enough to tear the paper, somebody has written four words. We are the payment.
a2_ledger: The pay-ledger comes off the table into Nyre's satchel: four pounds of paper and the entire second half of your contract. As it lifts clear the lamp above it gutters and goes out, as though the room had only been keeping the thing lit until somebody arrived to read it.
a2_take_iron: The ninth key-iron draws out of the lock as cold as the inside of a well and considerably heavier than its size argues for. The instant it clears the wards every lamp in the upper vault dips at once, together. Far below, something that had been counting steadily all day starts again from one.
a2_wrap: Salt-cloth, then oilcloth, then the middle of the pack, and the difference is immediate: the pressure behind everybody's eyes simply stops. Ilsabet says the thing nobody wanted said out loud, which is that the pressure was not the iron. It was being noticed through the iron.
a2_put_back: The iron goes back into the lock exactly as it was found, to the quarter turn. The lamps steady, the count somewhere below stops in the middle of a number, and the company stands in a room that has just declined, quite politely, to keep any of them.
a2_alcove: Behind the table is the clerk's alcove: a cot that has been slept in for months, a private tally scratched into the plaster in groups of nine, a jar of clean water. At floor level somebody has broken a hole through the wall, and warm air is coming up out of it.
a2_tally_private: The clerk's plaster tally is not a record of days at all, it is a record of deliveries, kept in groups of nine for eleven years by somebody with a steady and unhurried hand. In the final group there are only eight strokes cut into the plaster. Where the ninth stroke should be, he has written a single word in common speech, and the word is mine.
a2_hole: A lamp lowered on a bootlace shows eleven feet of broken wall and then a floor. On the floor there is a set of small neat footprints in the dust, and they go round in a circle, and they have gone round that same circle several hundred times without ever leaving it.
a2_lamps: The lamp gallery holds nine niches in a row with all nine lamps trimmed and full, and an oil store stacked to the roof behind them. A schedule board hangs on the wall in chalk, listing hours in a hand that takes its work seriously. On a bench beneath the board a lamp-keeper is asleep with a tally-book rising and falling on his chest.
a2_keeper: He is taken with a hand across his mouth and offers no resistance of any kind whatsoever. He is nineteen years old and a Warden's son by the belt he is wearing, and he is so thoroughly relieved to have been caught by people who ask questions that he starts answering before anybody has managed to put one to him. Nyre gets him a blanket before the interrogation begins.
a2_keeper_all: It comes out in a flat exhausted voice, the whole of it, with no prompting required after the first minute. The Compact is a contract, and the thing behind the Ninefold Door is neither dead nor intended ever to be dead. Eight irons hold the lid down, the ninth hand keeps the count and delivers what is owed, and the garrison, in the end, was simply what happened to be owed.
a2_keeper_route: He gives you the route and nothing else at all, gratefully. The great stair lies behind the ninth niche. There are two landings where nobody should stop for any reason whatsoever, and there is one hour of the day when the stair is in use by somebody else and must be left entirely alone.
a2_keeper_out: The promise is made out loud in front of witnesses, and Nyre writes it in her book, and the boy's whole posture changes as she does it. He gives you the route, the hours, the count, and a warning about the ninth hour delivered in the manner of a man confessing to a murder.
a2_terms: Woken civilly and offered a chair he is already sitting in, the keeper turns out to be a negotiator rather than a victim. He will give you the stair and the hours in exchange for one thing: the company carries a parcel out for him, unopened, and leaves it at a Ledger house.
a2_kill_keeper: The tally-book comes off a boy who never woke up. Nyre's face closes like a ledger at year end, Kettle finds something to look at on the far wall, and below in the hill the count falters on a number, holds for a moment, and then deliberately starts again from one.
a2_cloak: A keeper's cloak that does not fit anybody in the company, and a keeper's lamp held at a keeper's height. It is an adequate disguise against anything that counts by lamp-height, and no disguise at all against anything that counts by weight, and nobody says the second part out loud.
a2_board: The schedule board is chalk on slate, and it is entirely legible: nine niches, nine hours, the lamps to be trimmed on the hour without exception. The ninth hour has been ringed twice, and beside the ring the keeper has written four words in an extremely careful hand, which are do not be on the stair. Behind the ninth niche, the great stair goes down.
a2_ninth_hour: Four hours of waiting in the oil store, and then the ninth hour arrives exactly on schedule. Nine lamps are lifted off nine hooks by hands that nobody in the company looks at directly, a count starts down the stair, and the Ninth Sword steps into the forty paces of silence behind it.
a2_douse: Nine lamps are pinched out one after another, and the quality of the silence changes with every one of them. After the ninth, the hill is not quiet at all. It is attentive, in the way a room becomes attentive when everybody in it has stopped pretending to read.
a2_stair: The great stair of Kar Duhn lies behind the ninth niche, nine feet wide and cut by dwarves who expected regular traffic on it, dropping away in long flights into air that is warm and moving and ought to be neither. Somewhere far below it there is water. Above the water there is a smell like a forge that was left to go out very slowly.
e_a2_knock: Three knocks on dwarf bronze, and the door opens the rest of the way from the inside without anything visible touching it. A voice out of the dark invites the Ninth Sword in by the correct number, which is five, and none of the five is ever afterwards able to explain to anybody why they went.
e_a2_pinned: The haft holds the door for eleven seconds and then folds along its length, and the door closes back to its hand's width with a man still in the gap. The company ends up on both sides of a foot of bronze that will not move again for any lever anybody has left.
e_a2_chute_fall: The chute is taken the fast way, and the scree comes with you all at once, which is what scree does. The company arrives in the sump under four tons of moving stone in complete darkness, and that is not a fight, or an ambush, or in any way survivable.
e_a2_kettle_gone: The full ten minutes are kept exactly as agreed. Then the rope comes up with its end cut clean, no scout on it and no signal following it, and the company stands on a hillside at dusk with no way down that anybody trusts and a long walk to Gallowmere to explain the fact.
e_a2_outflow: The outflow is dived on one breath: eleven feet of cut stone, then a turn the wrong way, then the discovery that dwarves built their drains to be cleaned from the far end and never once from this one. The turn is too tight to reverse in.
e_a2_nest: Four pale drinkers are woken deliberately in a dark gallery by a company that had a plan and had rehearsed the plan twice. It survives contact for about eleven seconds, which is until the second one comes off the ceiling behind the line rather than in front of it. Afterwards the gallery is simply a larder with rather more in it than it had before.
e_a2_tooth: A hoard-tooth is lifted from the bay on the way past, which takes two seconds. The fourth drinker decides, on reflection, that it is worth bothering after all, and the salt line behind the company's feet turns out to have been laid for people who keep walking forward.
e_a2_challenge: A challenge is shouted down a dwarf corridor, and the answer comes back correctly in the Warden form, word for word, in the voice of the man whose shield is nailed to the gate post outside. The lamp keeps coming at walking pace, and nobody in the company manages to move.
e_a2_loot_home: Forty sets of Warden kit and a garrison's small coin go out by mule and sell in Gallowmere for genuinely good money inside a week. The commission is unfulfilled, and the pay-ledger is still lying open on its table under a lamp that nobody will trim again. The receipt in the Marshal's file records precisely what kind of company the Ninth Sword turned out to be.
e_a2_carry: A drained Warden is cut out of the barricade and carried toward daylight on a shield, on the sound principle that evidence wins arguments with Wardens. The thing on the shield waits until the second landing before demonstrating what it was so carefully kept alive in order to do.
e_a2_ask_too_long: The ninth question is asked aloud, and it is answered without hesitation. The answer is the company's own names, given back in the order they came through the door, together with the approximate hour of each arrival. Along the wall all eleven Wardens fold their hands in the same manner at the same moment, and then look up together.
e_a2_withdraw_rich: The remaining plate is loaded and walked out by the postern, declared honestly as salvage, and taxed at the proper rate. Redd reads the declaration without any expression at all before asking the only question that matters to him, which is where his pay-ledger has got to.
e_a2_mouth: The ninth iron is carried in the mouth, the way the bound man in the peat was carrying his, because both hands are needed on the rope. There is not time, afterwards, to spit it out and explain that the arrangement was purely practical, and the iron does not accept the distinction.
e_a2_hole: Eleven feet down a broken wall into a room where the footprints go round and round in a circle without ever leaving it. The circle turns out, on closer inspection with a lamp held low, to have a middle. The middle is occupied, and it has been occupied for eleven years, and it has been waiting for precisely this arrangement to present itself.
e_a2_reached: An arm goes through the hole in the wall to take up what is lying there, which is a lamp, and the lamp is still warm. A hand closes on the wrist out of the dark with the unhurried grip of something that has done this before and knows exactly how long it takes.
e_a2_fire: A light is put into an oil store holding a year's supply, and the gallery becomes a flue. The fire goes down the great stair ahead of the company, because that is where the air was going, and at the bottom of the stair it finds something that does not object to fire in the slightest.
e_a2_join: One hour in the file is agreed in exchange for safe passage down, and lamps are issued to everybody, and the count is taken up at the correct number. The hour ends precisely on schedule, exactly as the keeper promised it would. The company is not released, because the file's arithmetic contains no provision of any kind for anybody leaving it.
e_a2_douse: Nine lamps out, and the company waits in the dark to see who tends them. The answer comes up the stair without a light of its own, relights all nine from the bottom hook upward in the correct order, and takes the trimming of the wicks extremely seriously indeed.
e_a2_out: The stair is declined out loud, in front of witnesses, and the upper vault is walked back out through the gap in the great door with the sun coming up behind the moor. The ledger is delivered and the ninth iron is declared and taxed. The written report states plainly that the Ninth Sword did not go down, and Redd files it, and reads it twice.
